newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones mulls licensing Dow Industrials.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones mulls licensing Dow Industrials.

text.p: Dow Jones & Co Inc said it was discussing with various exchanges licensing its Dow Jones Industrial Average, arguably the most closely followed stock index in the world.

"We're studying the possibility, but we haven't drawn any conclusions," Dow Jones spokesman Roger May said. "This has a long history. We have studied the possibility in the past, and now we're studying it again.
"We had a policy a number of years ago very much against it," May said. "There was an effort to do it 15 years ago or so and we said 'no' -- but times changed."

"We've been talking to them (exchanges) about various index products -- our global products," May noted. "Part of our business is called Dow Jones Global Indexes, so obviously, when you're talking about these things, the subject of the Dow (Industrials) does come up.
"There's obviously interest out there in such a deal," he said.
The Chicago Mercantile Exchange, which in January listed futures and futures-options on the Dow Jones Taiwan index, said its talks with Dow Jones so far had focused on the global indexes.
"We've been discussing primarily about the Dow Jones Global Indexes -- about licensing them, like we did with the Taiwan index," a CME spokeswoman said.
The Chicago Board of Trade tried in the early 1980s to trade futures based on the Dow Jones Industrial Average, but Dow Jones sued the exchange to stop the plan. The CBOT eventually lost the lawsuit.
But the CBOT said Monday it was constantly reviewing its product line and was open to all possibilities.
"On an ongoing basis we review opportunities for a variety of products, including equity index," a CBOT spokesman said.
The index earlier this month set the financial markets astir as it pierced the 7,000 level, having gained nearly 2,000 points in just over a year.
